title: Follow the thread
principle: Listen for one concrete detail, then ask a question that gives the other person room to continue. A follow-up should come from what was actually said.
exercise: Repeat one key noun from their last sentence as a question, then pause.

title: Offer one true detail
principle: A brief, specific personal example can make a connection when it is relevant and genuinely yours; leave space for the other person to respond.
exercise: Share one detail from an approved story in two sentences, then invite their perspective.

title: Land one idea
principle: Choose the main point before adding context. A simple structure helps the listener follow without turning the exchange into a pitch.
exercise: Say the point in one sentence, add one example, then stop.

title: Check your understanding
principle: When meaning is uncertain, reflect the part you heard and ask whether you understood it. Treat interpretation as a question, never a fact about someone’s inner state.
exercise: Try: “It sounds like [observable point]—did I get that right?” Then listen.

title: Start with what is here
principle: Use a neutral, observable detail as a low-pressure opening, then let the other person choose whether to engage. Keep wit optional and kind.
exercise: Name a shared, visible detail and ask one open question about it.
